title: Kinematic properties of the Pauli equation
authors: E. E. Perepelkin, B. I. Sadovnikov, N. G. Inozemtseva, V. A. Svetovidov
abstract: Based on the Wigner-Vlasov formalism, this paper investigates the kinematic properties of the Pauli equation. It is shown that the probability current associated with the Pauli equation can be represented as a superposition of two currents with certain expansion coefficients. Each of these currents corresponds to a particular component of the spinor. The expansion coefficients effectively serve as weighting functions that determine the probability contribution of the corresponding spinor component. Therefore, each spin projection corresponds to its own probability flux. A new system of the Hamilton-Jacobi equations and also a system of motion equations in electromagnetic fields are obtained, taking into account the interaction between the spin and the magnetic field. To illustrate how these equations can be applied we have investigated the quantum system kinematics in detail using an exact solution of the Pauli equation in the presence of a uniform magnetic field and an asymmetric quadratic potential.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the kinematics of the Pauli equation using advanced formalisms like Wigner-Vlasov. It demonstrates that the spinorial nature leads to a splitting of probability flux and derives coupled Hamilton-Jacobi equations for both the Pauli and Schrödinger systems. The paper is significant for establishing deep mathematical consistency between these fundamental quantum descriptions in electromagnetic environments.
main_problem: The paper investigates the kinematic properties of quantum systems governed by the Pauli equation, comparing its dynamics to those described by the Schrödinger equation.
main_result: It establishes that the probability flux associated with the Pauli equation splits into two components corresponding to its spinor structure, and derives analogous Hamilton-Jacobi equations for both systems.
method: The analysis heavily utilizes the Wigner-Vlasov formalism, employing Helmholtz decomposition and deriving coupled sets of differential equations for potentials and fluxes.
model_or_system: The primary model is a spin-1/2 particle governed by the Pauli equation in external electromagnetic fields. The comparison system is the standard Schrödinger equation counterpart.
key_observables: Probability current flux ($\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2$), quantum potential ($Q$), Hamilton-Jacobi functions ($H_n$), and magnetic moment ($\mathbf{\mu}_s$).
important_parameters: Uniform magnetic fields, asymmetric quadratic potentials, and the spin coupling constant (related to the Bohr magneton).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on specific gauge choices (e.g., Lorenz $\Psi$-gauge) and approximations within the Wigner-Vlasov expansion.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the probability flux distribution ($v_\lambdaho$) for different spin components ($\lambda$), showing directional flow relative to color coding.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first introducing the Wigner-Vlasov formalism, deriving analogues of H-J equations and motion equations (Theorem 1), then constructing a formal link between Pauli and Schrödinger dynamics (Theorem 2), establishing field consistency with Maxwell's equations (Theorem 4), and concluding with explicit solutions for specific potentials.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical connection drawn between the spinorial nature of the Pauli equation and classical/semi-classical Hamilton-Jacobi mechanics is highly relevant for understanding quantum dynamics in external fields, bridging foundational QM theory with semi-classical methods.
